problems.problem: Dead vertical band: the product base sits at y=893 while the translucent teal block starts only at y=1010, leaving a ~117px empty grey gap under the shoe, and the block's hard left edge at x=300 stops in mid-field with no alignment to the shoe (bbox x 55-705) or to the text column (x=734). The lower third reads as an unanchored rectangle instead of part of the ' Margin Catalogue' grid.

The ink hairline (shape at x=760) pierces the word FOOTWEAR (text bbox x 734-1006, y 576-606) between the 'F' and the first 'O', and continues through the teal block to y=1320. text_product_overlap is false and the column concept is 'beside', so a rule crossing the headline glyphs is an execution flaw, not the declared separation.

The promised 'clearly readable fine vertical fluting' of the frosted acrylic panel is barely perceptible: the field renders as a near-flat grey gradient with a faint vertical streak, so the poster loses its material story and reads as a plain wall with a pasted cutout, unlike the tactile surfaces of the references.

In the contact detail crop [0,753,785,1003] a soft contact shadow IS present at the cleat line (base_y 893, offset_y 0 correct), but at opacity 0.5 with blur 14 under only a 177px-wide footprint it is too faint for the 652px-wide sole; heel and forefoot cleats still appear to hover slightly above the grey field.

Hierarchy inside the right column is thin: 44px title versus 40px logo with a 94px gap leaves the column sparse against the large negative space; the tracked 'Nike' in Baskerville reads as a second headline rather than a stacked brand mark, weakening the catalogue column idea.

changes.value: Cool fog-grey ribbed frosted acrylic panel with pronounced fine vertical fluting clearly visible across the whole sheet, pale paper beneath, soft diffuse even cool north light, gentle translucency glowing inside the ribs, quiet matte surface, subtle vertical grain gradient, no horizon, no objects
